newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt sees 1998 Sydney airport decision.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt sees 1998 Sydney airport decision.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said on Monday he did not expect a decision to be made on the location of a second Sydney airport before next year.
"I don't expect a decision to be made until early next year," Sharp told reporters.

Sharp said that the government expected to release "in the near future" an environmental impact study of proposals for the second airport at either Badgery's Creek in Sydney's west or Holsworthy in Sydney's south.
The privatisation of the lease on Sydney's existing airport at Mascot is on hold until a second airport decision is made.
Sharp called a news conference after a coalition of Sydney local councils met earlier on Monday to oppose the proposed locations of the planned Sydney airport.
The minister said the government had to ensure that a second airport should be built as Sydney's main airport at Mascot was near to its capacity and that there should be no further delay.

"If we were to restart the process all over again, you will only add further years to the whole process. You will create a further crisis, because the growth of aviation in Australia is such that Mascot will reach a maximum capacity within the forseeable future," Sharp said.
Sydney is Australia's main tourism and business gateway.
Australia first introduced a plan in 1946 to build a second airport in Sydney.
"This process started 51 years ago, several governments have tried and baulked at the final decision," Sharp said.

"These further delays would only add to the cost of building the project and reduce the opportunity to further our tourism industry and reduce the opportunity to create jobs," Sharp said. The previous Labor government had planned to build a second airport at Badgerys Creek in time for the expected flood of tourists for the 2000 Sydney Olympic Games.
